page: Amazon Web Services m5d.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs, which correspond to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, and a 35 MB L3 cache. It includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 300 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core CPU capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6989.22 and a passmark CPU score of 7396.11. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a geekbench single-core score of 1013.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1326.19. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 376.29 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 48.61 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance struggles with heavy computational tasks, exhibiting poor performance in medium-model LLM inference with 9.97 tokens/sec prompt processing and weak performance in single-threaded decompression and image processing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m5d.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads requiring high-speed local NVMe storage. The inclusion of the 300 GB local NVMe SSD provides a cost-effective alternative to relying solely on network-attached storage for temporary data. This hardware profile is well-suited for database operations, redis caching, static web serving, and software compilation, where its average database operations and redis SET performance can be leveraged. It is less suitable for modern machine learning inference or compute-intensive single-threaded applications.
description: Amazon Web Services m5d.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it includes a 300 GB local NVMe SSD instance store and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark data shows average multi-core CPU and memory performance, with a passmark CPU score of 7396.11 and a redis SET throughput of 6.88 million operations per second. However, single-core performance and LLM inference speeds are weak to poor. The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is driven by its integrated local NVMe storage, which eliminates the need for external storage for transient data. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, database operations, static web serving, and software compilation, while being less optimal for compute-heavy or single-threaded tasks.
